newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK PUTS IBID IN RECEIVERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK PUTS IBID IN RECEIVERSHIP.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) placed in receivership the private International Bank for Investment and Development (IBID) to due to a danger of insolvency, a BNB official said on Thursday.
"The BNB board decided to put in receivership the International Bank for Investment and Development because of a danger of insolvency," the BNB official told Reuters.

The bank posted a negative capital-to-risks assets ratio of 18 percent and suffured liquidity shortage as a result of after extending a high amount of non-performing loans distributed among its sharehodlers, the official said.
The BNB has cited that most of the loans were extended in violation of the bank supervision regulations, the official said, declining to elaborate.
The IBID was set up in 1992 as a joint Bulgarian-American bank.
In 1995 the majority stake was acquired by Bulgaria's Compact holding, headed by a businessman Ivan Evlogiev and controlled by the Compact group private companies.

Since May 17 the BNB had placed in receivership and had filed inslovency suits through the court against 16 banks. Four banks have been declared insolvent so far and one was sold to a foreign investor. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
